newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Dutch say no EU beef reform accord in 1st half '97.
newsitem.headline: Dutch say no EU beef reform accord in 1st half '97.

text.p: Further beef reforms will not be agreed during the six-months Dutch EU Presidency ending on June 30, Dutch Farm Minister Jozias Van Aartsen said on Monday.

"We want to make as much progress as possible so that a decision can be taken under the Luxembourg EU Presidency in the autumn," Van Aartsen told a news conference after a meeting of EU farm ministers.
The long term reforms are intended to cut production to bring it into line with a drop in demand following a public health scare over mad cow disease which erupted in March 1996.

Van Aartsen, presenting the Dutch EU Presidency's farm programme, stressed the need to quickly agree proposals on beef labelling and cattle eartagging, passports and computer registers to identify and track animal movements.
"This is the only way to restore consumer confidence in beef and beef products," he said.

Dairy reforms will be discussed at an informal meeting of EU farm ministers in Domburg, Zeeland, from May 25 - 27, Van Aartsen said, adding "It will be on the basis of a European Commission (market analysis) paper and we hope for a frank exchange of views."

The current EU milk production quota system only expires in March 2000 but the Dutch want to get agreement before the next round of world farm trade talks starts in 1999 and the EU's enlargement eastwards early next century.
On animal welfare, the Dutch are seeking to obtain agreement on standards for rest centres and lorries used during long distance tranport of farm animals.
The Dutch have also planned a meeting between EU farm ministers and their counterparts from 10 eastern European countries which have applied for EU membership.
The meeting, scheduled during an EU Farm Council on March 17 - 18 will discuss veterinary issues.
